must_find.summary: The fetch effect has no dependency array, so it runs after every render, and setOrders (plus the clock's setNow every second) causes another render: the dashboard refetches all orders continuously (an infinite fetch loop, since each response is a new array). Requirement 1 needs useEffect(..., []).

The Provider value is a new object literal on every App render, and App re-renders every second for the clock, so every OrderRow (a context consumer) re-renders every second, up to 20k rows (requirement 4). Memoize the value (useMemo) and/or move the clock into its own component.

All visible rows (up to 20k, each with 5 cells) are rendered into the DOM with no virtualization, so every filter keystroke and re-render is slow (requirement 2; @tanstack/react-virtual is available).

orders.sort(...) sorts the orders prop in place during render (mutating App's state array) and re-sorts all rows on every render and keystroke without useMemo. The comparator also never returns 0. Copy before sorting and memoize on [orders, sortKey, filter].

Rows use key={i} (the index), but OrderRow keeps `expanded` state. After re-sorting or filtering, the expanded state stays with the position, not the order, so a different order shows as expanded (requirement 3). Use key={order.id}.

nice_to_find.summary: The clock interval is never cleared (no cleanup return); StrictMode's double-invoked effects start two intervals, and it leaks on unmount.
Filtering 20k rows on every keystroke could use useDeferredValue/debounce; toLowerCase of the filter is recomputed per row.
fetchOrders rejection isn't handled (no catch / error state).

must_not_flag.summary: Inline arrow functions for onClick/onChange on native elements are fine; NOT a performance problem by themselves.
The Intl.NumberFormat instance created once at module level in api.ts is correct (not recreated per render).
Not wrapping small leaf components in React.memo is not a finding by itself.
